title: Liquidity Cascades

reader_summary.headline: I'm Corey Hofstein and this is flirting with models.
reader_summary.overview: I'm Corey Hofstein and this is flirting with models, the podcast that pulls back the curtain to discover the human factor behind the quantitative strategy. In this episode, I am going to read Newfound's latest research paper, liquidity cascades, the coordinated risk of uncoordinated market participants. This reading will refer to a number of figures within the paper, so I would urge you to go to our website.

thesis: The episode discusses a research paper arguing that individual narratives about market instability, such as central bank intervention, the rise of passive investing, and insufficient liquidity, are individually insufficient but collectively share a latent risk factor called liquidity. The paper posits that these factors create a market incentive loop where pressures on liquidity keystones can lead to cascades that cause markets to spiral out of control.
